Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

too adverb

more than enough

also too much, too many, excessively, overly

classical

Mart. 1.15.12: sēra nimis vīta est crāstina
Ter. And. 61: nē quid nimis

nimis

adverb

too, too much

Before adjectives and adverbs (nimis graviter, too harshly: Ter. Heaut. 5.5.1, Lewis & Short); with a genitive, too much of (nimis īnsidiārum: Cic. Or. 170). Nōn nimis is “not very” (Cic. Att. 7.24.1, Lewis & Short). Latin often says “too” with the comparative alone: sērius, too late (Traupman 87); pede major, too big for the foot (see too big).

Other words

  • nimium — too, too much

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 1.10: nimium diū (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fam. 16.18.3: nimium est aquae; Traupman 88: too soon, nimium citō

    The same word as nimis, in all its uses (Lewis & Short); as a noun with a genitive, too much: nimium est aquae, there’s too much water.

Examples

  • nōn est, crēde mihi, sapientis dīcere "vīvam": sēra nimis vīta est crāstina: vīve hodiē

    believe me, it is not wise to say ‘I shall live’: tomorrow’s life is too late; live todayMart. 1.15.11–12

  • Nē quid nimis.

    Nothing too much.Ter. And. 61

  • nunc quidem etiam nimium est aquae

    just now there’s even too much waterCic. Fam. 16.18.3

See also it’s too early, too big, too small, that’s enough!, also.

SourcesLewis & Short: nimis · Lewis & Short: nimius
